claim: Aven harbors an N-terminal RGG/RG motif.
source: Aven harbors an N-terminal RGG/RG motif (Thandapani et al., 2013), a nuclear export sequence (Esmaili et al., 2010), and a predicted BH3 domain (Hawley et al., 2012) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Thandapani et al., 2013.

claim: Aven harbors a nuclear export sequence.
source: Aven harbors an N-terminal RGG/RG motif (Thandapani et al., 2013), a nuclear export sequence (Esmaili et al., 2010), and a predicted BH3 domain (Hawley et al., 2012) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Esmaili et al., 2010.

claim: Aven harbors a predicted BH3 domain.
source: Aven harbors an N-terminal RGG/RG motif (Thandapani et al., 2013), a nuclear export sequence (Esmaili et al., 2010), and a predicted BH3 domain (Hawley et al., 2012) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hawley et al., 2012.

claim: GST-AvenRGG/RG fusion protein was methylated by PRMT1 in vitro.
source: The GST-AvenRGG/RG fusion protein migrated as a doublet and was methylated by PRMT1, while GST alone was not methylated (Figure 1B, lanes 5, 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: GST alone was not methylated by PRMT1 in vitro.
source: The GST-AvenRGG/RG fusion protein migrated as a doublet and was methylated by PRMT1, while GST alone was not methylated (Figure 1B, lanes 5, 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PRMT1 co-immunoprecipitates with Myc-Aven in HEK293T cells.
source: PRMT1 was present in anti-Myc immunoprecipitates of the Myc-Aven-transfected cells, but not in the empty vector-transfected cells (Figure 1C, lanes 3, 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Myc-Aven is arginine methylated in PRMT1-proficient cells but not in PRMT1-deficient cells.
source: We observed that Myc-Aven was arginine methylated in PRMT1-proficient, but not in PRMT1-deficient cells (Figure 1D, compare lanes 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Myc-Aven was arginine methylated in PRMT1-proficient MEFs but not in PRMT1-deficient MEFs.
source: Myc-Aven was arginine methylated in PRMT1-proficient, but not in PRMT1-deficient cells (Figure 1E, compare lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data from conditional PRMT1FL/−;CreERT MEFs shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Endogenous Aven is asymmetrically dimethylated by PRMT1.
source: Conditional PRMT1FL/−;CreERT MEFs were used for Aven immunoprecipitations and indeed endogenous Aven was asymmetrically dimethylated by PRMT1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data from conditional PRMT1FL/−;CreERT MEFs shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Endogenous Aven migrates at approximately 50 kDa.
source: Endogenous Aven migrates at ∼50 kDa (Figure 1F), while myc-Aven was generated with multiple Myc tags to avoid overlap with heavy chain of IgG during immunoprecipitation and migrated at ∼70 kDa (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Myc-Aven migrates at approximately 70 kDa.
source: Endogenous Aven migrates at ∼50 kDa (Figure 1F), while myc-Aven was generated with multiple Myc tags to avoid overlap with heavy chain of IgG during immunoprecipitation and migrated at ∼70 kDa (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figures 1C-E.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified dimethylation of Aven R37, R63, and R66.
source: We identified the dimethylation of Aven R37, R63, and R66 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified dimethylation of Aven R8, R11, and R50.
source: Moreover, we also identified the dimethylation of R8, R11, R50, as well as the monomethylation of R5, R8, R28, and R37.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified monomethylation of Aven R5, R8, R28, and R37.
source: Moreover, we also identified the dimethylation of R8, R11, R50, as well as the monomethylation of R5, R8, R28, and R37.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: Arginines R5, R8, R11, R37, R50, and R63 are conserved in murines.
source: Arginines R5, R8, R11, R37, R50, and R63 are also conserved in murines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Aven RGG/RG motif is methylated by PRMT1 on conserved arginines.
source: Taken together, these findings demonstrate that the Aven RGG/RG motif is methylated by PRMT1 on conserved arginines.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro methylation assays, co-immunoprecipitation experiments, and mass spectrometry data.

claim: AvenΔRGG was not recognized by ASYM25b antibody.
source: AvenΔRGG was not recognized by ASYM25b, confirming that all the methylarginines reside in the N-terminus of Aven (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: All methylarginines in Aven reside in the N-terminus.
source: AvenΔRGG was not recognized by ASYM25b, confirming that all the methylarginines reside in the N-terminus of Aven (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that AvenΔRGG (lacking amino acids 1-73) is not recognized by ASYM25b antibody.

claim: AvenΔRGG was able to activate ATM comparably to wild-type Aven.
source: AvenΔRGG was able to activate ATM, comparably to wild-type Aven and deletion of the RGG/RG motif did not interfere with its ability to oligomerize (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deletion of the RGG/RG motif did not interfere with Aven's ability to oligomerize.
source: AvenΔRGG was able to activate ATM, comparably to wild-type Aven and deletion of the RGG/RG motif did not interfere with its ability to oligomerize (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Aven is predominantly localized in the cytoplasm with some weak nuclear staining.
source: Aven is predominantly localized in the cytoplasm with some weak nuclear staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), as reported previously (Chau et al., 2000), and FLAG-AvenΔRGG had the same cellular localization pattern as wild-type Aven (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and a citation to Chau et al., 2000.

claim: FLAG-AvenΔRGG had the same cellular localization pattern as wild-type Aven.
source: Aven is predominantly localized in the cytoplasm with some weak nuclear staining (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), as reported previously (Chau et al., 2000), and FLAG-AvenΔRGG had the same cellular localization pattern as wild-type Aven (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Aven bound the sc1 wild-type G4 RNA but not a mutant sc1 RNA sequence.
source: Aven bound the sc1 wild-type G4 RNA, but not a mutant sc1 RNA sequence that is predicted not to form the G4 structure (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: FLAG-Aven bound the sc1 G4 structure but FLAG-AvenΔRGG did not.
source: FLAG-Aven, but not FLAG-AvenΔRGG, bound the sc1 G4 structure indicating that the RGG/RG motif is necessary for binding (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The RGG/RG motif is necessary for Aven binding to the sc1 G4 structure.
source: FLAG-Aven, but not FLAG-AvenΔRGG, bound the sc1 G4 structure indicating that the RGG/RG motif is necessary for binding (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that FLAG-AvenΔRGG (lacking the RGG/RG motif) does not bind the sc1 G4 structure.

claim: Aven bound equally well to biotinylated sc1 G4 RNA from wild-type or PRMT1-depleted cells.
source: Aven bound equally well to biotinylated sc1 G4 RNA from wild-type or PRMT1-depleted cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Aven RGG/RG motif with or without asymmetric dimethylarginines bound fluoresceinated sc1 G4 RNA with a Kd of approximately 80-90 nM.
source: RGG/RG motif whether harboring arginine or asymmetric dimethylarginines bound a fluoresceinated sc1 G4 RNA, induced to fold into a G4 structure prior to binding, with same relative affinities with a Kd of ∼80–90 nM (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence-based RNA binding assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Aven DiRGG peptides with and without asymmetric dimethylarginines bound fluoresceinated sc1 G4 RNA with a Kd of approximately 175-200 nM.
source: Another set of peptides spanning the DiRGG motif of Aven with and without asymmetric dimethylarginines also bound the fluoresceinated sc1 G4 RNA with lower affinity than the TriRG peptides (Kd of ∼175–200 nM, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that several RGG/RG motifs in Aven are able to bind RNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence-based RNA binding assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Several RGG/RG motifs in Aven are able to bind RNA.
source: Another set of peptides spanning the DiRGG motif of Aven with and without asymmetric dimethylarginines also bound the fluoresceinated sc1 G4 RNA with lower affinity than the TriRG peptides (Kd of ∼175–200 nM, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting that several RGG/RG motifs in Aven are able to bind RNA.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that both TriRG and DiRGG peptides bind RNA.

claim: Aven is an RBP that interacts with G4 RNA sequences via its RGG/RG motifs independent of arginine methylation.
source: These finding show that Aven is an RBP that interacts with G4 RNA sequences via its RGG/RG motifs independent of arginine methylation.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assays showing that Aven binds G4 RNA equally well in PRMT1-proficient and PRMT1-deficient conditions.

claim: Arginine methylation is known to regulate protein-protein interactions with Tudor domain-containing proteins.
source: Arginine methylation is known to regulate protein–protein interactions with Tudor domain-containing proteins (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2011.

claim: Methylated RGG/RG motifs are known to interact specifically with the Tudor domains of TDRD3, SMN, and SPF30.
source: Although there are many Tudor domain-containing proteins, methylated RGG/RG motifs are known to interact specifically with the Tudor domains of TDRD3, SMN, and SPF30 (Selenko et al., 2001; Cote and Richard, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Selenko et al., 2001 and Cote and Richard, 2005.

claim: FLAG-Aven interacted with GST-TDRD3 and GST-SMN Tudor domains but FLAG-AvenΔRGG did not.
source: FLAG-Aven, but not FLAG-AvenΔRGG, interacted with the GST Tudor domains of TDRD3 and SMN, suggesting that TDRD3 and SMN Tudor domains interact with the Aven RGG/RG motif (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: TDRD3 and SMN Tudor domains interact with the Aven RGG/RG motif.
source: FLAG-Aven, but not FLAG-AvenΔRGG, interacted with the GST Tudor domains of TDRD3 and SMN, suggesting that TDRD3 and SMN Tudor domains interact with the Aven RGG/RG motif (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that FLAG-AvenΔRGG (lacking the RGG/RG motif) does not interact with TDRD3 and SMN Tudor domains.

claim: GST-SPF30 Tudor domain had a weak interaction with FLAG-Aven but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG.
source: GST-SPF30 Tudor domain had a weak interaction with FLAG-Aven, but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Endogenous TDRD3 co-immunoprecipitates with FLAG-Aven but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG.
source: Endogenous TDRD3 and SMN co-IP with FLAG-Aven, but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Endogenous SMN co-immunoprecipitates with FLAG-Aven but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG.
source: Endogenous TDRD3 and SMN co-IP with FLAG-Aven, but not with FLAG-AvenΔRGG (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PRMT1 depletion reduced the interaction between FLAG-Aven and SMN and TDRD3.
source: Indeed, cells depleted of PRMT1 showed reduced interaction between FLAG-Aven and SMN and TDRD3, as compared to the control (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The ability of SMN and TDRD3 to co-immunoprecipitate with endogenous Aven was lost in PRMT1-deficient cells.
source: The ability of SMN and TDRD3 to co-immunoprecipitate with endogenous Aven was lost in PRMT1-deficient cells (+OHT; Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data from conditional PRMT1FL/−;CreERT MEFs shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Methylation of the RGG/RG motif is required for interaction between the Aven/TDRD3 and Aven/SMN complexes.
source: These findings confirm that methylation of the RGG/RG motif is required for interaction between the Aven/TDRD3 and Aven/SMN complexes.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing that PRMT1 depletion reduces Aven interactions with TDRD3 and SMN.

claim: Approximately 23% of the 146 proteins enriched with Aven but not AvenΔRGG were ribosomal proteins.
source: Of the 146 proteins enriched with Aven, but not AvenΔRGG, ∼23% were ribosomal proteins and ∼10% were RBPs, their association is likely RNA-dependent (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by SILAC mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: Approximately 10% of the 146 proteins enriched with Aven but not AvenΔRGG were RBPs.
source: Of the 146 proteins enriched with Aven, but not AvenΔRGG, ∼23% were ribosomal proteins and ∼10% were RBPs, their association is likely RNA-dependent (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by SILAC mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: The association of ribosomal proteins and RBPs with Aven is likely RNA-dependent.
source: Of the 146 proteins enriched with Aven, but not AvenΔRGG, ∼23% were ribosomal proteins and ∼10% were RBPs, their association is likely RNA-dependent (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the nature of the proteins identified.

claim: Aven associates with ribosomes in an RGG/RG motif-dependent manner.
source: These data suggested that Aven, but not AvenΔRGG, associates with ribosomal proteins and/or RNP complexes, thereby implying that Aven associates with ribosomes in an RGG/RG motif-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from SILAC data showing enrichment of ribosomal proteins with Aven but not AvenΔRGG.

claim: Endogenous Aven co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions.
source: Aven and PRMT1 co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions with rpS6, while β-tubulin was restricted to the lighter fractions of the sucrose gradient corresponding to cytoplasmic mRNP fractions (Figure 4B, fractions 11 to 16).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: PRMT1 co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions.
source: Aven and PRMT1 co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions with rpS6, while β-tubulin was restricted to the lighter fractions of the sucrose gradient corresponding to cytoplasmic mRNP fractions (Figure 4B, fractions 11 to 16).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: β-tubulin was restricted to the lighter fractions of the sucrose gradient corresponding to cytoplasmic mRNP fractions.
source: Aven and PRMT1 co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions with rpS6, while β-tubulin was restricted to the lighter fractions of the sucrose gradient corresponding to cytoplasmic mRNP fractions (Figure 4B, fractions 11 to 16).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: FLAG-Aven co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions while FLAG-AvenΔRGG was more shifted towards the lighter fractions.
source: FLAG-Aven co-sedimented with the heavier polysomal fractions, while FLAG-AvenΔRGG was more shifted towards the lighter fractions (Figure 4C,D) and this was quantified (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figures 4C, 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The RGG/RG motif of Aven is required for its recruitment to polysomes.
source: These findings suggest that RGG/RG motif of Aven is required for its recruitment to polysomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that FLAG-AvenΔRGG (lacking the RGG/RG motif) is shifted towards lighter fractions compared to FLAG-Aven.

claim: PRMT1 depletion did not have a major effect on the monosome/polysome ratio.
source: Similar to what has been reported in fission yeast (Bachand and Silver, 2004), PRMT1 depletion did not have a major effect on the monosome/polysome ratio, thus, indicating that PRMT1 does not exert a major impact on global protein synthesis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome profile data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and a citation to Bachand and Silver, 2004.

claim: PRMT1 does not exert a major impact on global protein synthesis.
source: Similar to what has been reported in fission yeast (Bachand and Silver, 2004), PRMT1 depletion did not have a major effect on the monosome/polysome ratio, thus, indicating that PRMT1 does not exert a major impact on global protein synthesis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PRMT1 depletion does not affect the monosome/polysome ratio.

claim: PRMT1 depletion shifted FLAG-Aven into the lighter fractions.
source: Nonetheless, PRMT1 depletion shifted FLAG-Aven into the lighter fractions, as compared to a control (compare Figure 4E and Figure 4G, quantified in Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figures 4E, 4G, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Puromycin leads to redistribution of both FLAG-Aven and rpS6 towards the lighter fractions.
source: We confirmed that Aven does not co-sediment with mRNPs other than polysomes by showing that puromycin, an aminonucleoside antibiotic that dissociates polysomes (Blobel and Sabatini, 1971), leads to redistribution of both FLAG-Aven and rpS6 towards the lighter fractions corresponding to free ribosomal subunits, monosomes, and cytoplasmic mRNPs (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4F and a citation to Blobel and Sabatini, 1971.

claim: Puromycin is an aminonucleoside antibiotic that dissociates polysomes.
source: We confirmed that Aven does not co-sediment with mRNPs other than polysomes by showing that puromycin, an aminonucleoside antibiotic that dissociates polysomes (Blobel and Sabatini, 1971), leads to redistribution of both FLAG-Aven and rpS6 towards the lighter fractions corresponding to free ribosomal subunits, monosomes, and cytoplasmic mRNPs (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Blobel and Sabatini, 1971.

claim: The arginine methylation of the Aven RGG/RG motif by PRMT1 is required for the association of Aven with polysomes.
source: Taken together, our findings suggest that the arginine methylation of the Aven RGG/RG motif by PRMT1 is required for the association of Aven with polysomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation experiments showing that PRMT1 depletion shifts Aven to lighter fractions.

claim: Depletion of both TDRD3 and SMN reduced polysomal association of Aven.
source: In contrast, depletion of both TDRD3 and SMN, but not single TDRD3 or SMN depletion (data not shown) reduced polysomal association of Aven, as compared to the control (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by polysome fractionation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Single TDRD3 or SMN depletion did not reduce polysomal association of Aven.
source: In contrast, depletion of both TDRD3 and SMN, but not single TDRD3 or SMN depletion (data not shown) reduced polysomal association of Aven, as compared to the control (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text but data is not shown.

claim: TDRD3 and SMN are required for the recruitment of Aven to polysomes.
source: These findings suggest that TDRD3 and SMN are required for the recruitment of Aven to polysomes, whereby these proteins likely play a redundant role.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that depletion of both TDRD3 and SMN reduces polysomal association of Aven.

claim: TDRD3 and SMN likely play a redundant role in recruiting Aven to polysomes.
source: These findings suggest that TDRD3 and SMN are required for the recruitment of Aven to polysomes, whereby these proteins likely play a redundant role.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observation that single depletion of TDRD3 or SMN does not affect Aven polysomal association, but double depletion does.

claim: RGG/RG motifs are encoded by G-rich sequences.
source: Next, we reasoned that since RGG/RG motifs are encoded by G-rich sequences (codons: Gly GGN; Arg CGN or AGA/G), it is likely that certain mRNAs encoding RGG/RG motif-containing proteins may occasionally comprise a PG4 sequences (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge of the genetic code.

claim: Certain mRNAs encoding RGG/RG motif-containing proteins may occasionally comprise PG4 sequences.
source: Next, we reasoned that since RGG/RG motifs are encoded by G-rich sequences (codons: Gly GGN; Arg CGN or AGA/G), it is likely that certain mRNAs encoding RGG/RG motif-containing proteins may occasionally comprise a PG4 sequences (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the G-rich nature of RGG/RG encoding sequences.

claim: Bioinformatic search revealed approximately 1600 PG4 in human ORFs.
source: To identify these RGG/RG encoding sequences and to identify all PG4 sequences in the coding sequences, we performed a bioinformatic search for PG4 sequences in mRNA-coding regions (Gx-N1-7-Gx-N1-7-Gx-N1-7-Gx, where x ≥ 3 and N is any of the nucleotides [A, C, G, or U]), and it revealed ∼1600 PG4 in human ORFs (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: Human KMT2A (MLL1) has a PG4 sequence at nucleotide 223-253 that encodes a glycine-rich sequence.
source: KMT2A (MLL1) has a PG4 sequence (nucleotide 223–253) that encodes a glycine-rich sequence (AGSSGAGVPGG, Figure 5B; cG/cC score of 2.975, Figure 5—source data 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: Human KMT2B (MLL4) has 3 PG4 sequences at nucleotides 262-287, 3139-3166, and 6274-6301.
source: KMT2B (MLL4) has 3 PG4 sequences (nucleotides 262–287; 3139–3166; 6274–6301) that encode an RGG/RG motif (RVQRGRGRG, Figure 5B; cG/cC score of 2.796, Figure 5—source data 1), a glycine-rich (RGAGAGGPRE; cG/cC score of 1.887, Figure 5—source data 1), an alanine-glycine-rich (RAGVLGAAGD; cG/cC score of 2.468, Figure 5—source data 1) sequences
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: Aven bound MLL1 PG4 RNA sequences in an RGG/RG motif-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, Aven bound either MLL1 or MLL4 PG4 RNA sequences in the RGG/RG motif-dependent manner, but not to those harboring guanine to adenine mutants (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figures 5C-F.

claim: Aven bound MLL4 PG4 RNA sequences in an RGG/RG motif-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, Aven bound either MLL1 or MLL4 PG4 RNA sequences in the RGG/RG motif-dependent manner, but not to those harboring guanine to adenine mutants (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figures 5C-F.

claim: Aven did not bind MLL1 or MLL4 PG4 RNA sequences harboring guanine to adenine mutants.
source: Indeed, Aven bound either MLL1 or MLL4 PG4 RNA sequences in the RGG/RG motif-dependent manner, but not to those harboring guanine to adenine mutants (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA binding assay data shown in Figures 5C-F.

claim: Anti-FLAG immunoprecipitations of FLAG-Aven expressing cells enriched approximately 30-fold for the MLL4 G4 sequence.
source: Anti-FLAG immunoprecipitations of FLAG-Aven expressing cells, but not pcDNA3.1 or FLAG-AvenΔRGG-transfected cells, enriched ∼30-fold for the MLL4 G4 sequence, whereas an RNA region 300 nucleotides downstream was not enriched (noG4; Figure 5G, right panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: An RNA region 300 nucleotides downstream of the MLL4 G4 sequence was not enriched in FLAG-Aven immunoprecipitations.
source: Anti-FLAG immunoprecipitations of FLAG-Aven expressing cells, but not pcDNA3.1 or FLAG-AvenΔRGG-transfected cells, enriched ∼30-fold for the MLL4 G4 sequence, whereas an RNA region 300 nucleotides downstream was not enriched (noG4; Figure 5G, right panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: MLL1 G4 sequence was enriched approximately fivefold in FLAG-Aven immunoprecipitations.
source: MLL1 G4 sequence was also enriched (∼fivefold) in FLAG-Aven immunoprecipitations, but not a region without G4 motifs (noG4) (Figure 5G, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: A region without G4 motifs in MLL1 was not enriched in FLAG-Aven immunoprecipitations.
source: MLL1 G4 sequence was also enriched (∼fivefold) in FLAG-Aven immunoprecipitations, but not a region without G4 motifs (noG4) (Figure 5G, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: MLL1 and MLL4 PG4 sequences associated with immunoprecipitated endogenous Aven.
source: Photocrosslinking immunoprecipitations assays confirmed that MLL1 and MLL4 PG4 sequences associated with IP endogenous Aven, but not immunoglobulin G control albeit with a lower affinity (∼fourfold to sixfold, Figure 5H) than with overexpressing FLAG-Aven (Figure 5G) and that ultraviolet light was required for this association (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Ultraviolet light was required for the association of MLL1 and MLL4 PG4 sequences with endogenous Aven.
source: Photocrosslinking immunoprecipitations assays confirmed that MLL1 and MLL4 PG4 sequences associated with IP endogenous Aven, but not immunoglobulin G control albeit with a lower affinity (∼fourfold to sixfold, Figure 5H) than with overexpressing FLAG-Aven (Figure 5G) and that ultraviolet light was required for this association (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Aven is associated in vivo with the PG4s of MLL1 and MLL4.
source: These findings demonstrate that Aven is associated in vivo with the PG4s of MLL1 and MLL4.
evidence: The claim is supported by photocrosslinking immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: In-line probing experiments showed increased cleavage in the predicted loops of MLL1 and MLL4 PG4 when incubated in K+ compared to Li+.
source: Using MLL1 and MLL4 PG4, we observed increased cleavage in the predicted loops of the formed G4, when incubated in K+ compared to Li+. However, no such difference was observed for a mutant RNA, where guanines were replaced with adenines (Figure 5I), confirming that the PG4 of MLL1 and MLL4 form G4 RNA structures.
evidence: The claim is supported by in-line probing data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: No difference in cleavage was observed for a mutant RNA where guanines were replaced with adenines.
source: Using MLL1 and MLL4 PG4, we observed increased cleavage in the predicted loops of the formed G4, when incubated in K+ compared to Li+. However, no such difference was observed for a mutant RNA, where guanines were replaced with adenines (Figure 5I), confirming that the PG4 of MLL1 and MLL4 form G4 RNA structures.
evidence: The claim is supported by in-line probing data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The PG4 of MLL1 and MLL4 form G4 RNA structures.
source: Using MLL1 and MLL4 PG4, we observed increased cleavage in the predicted loops of the formed G4, when incubated in K+ compared to Li+. However, no such difference was observed for a mutant RNA, where guanines were replaced with adenines (Figure 5I), confirming that the PG4 of MLL1 and MLL4 form G4 RNA structures.
evidence: The claim is supported by in-line probing data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Aven is required for the proliferation of T-ALL cells.
source: Aven is required for the proliferation of T-ALL cells (Eismann et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Eismann et al., 2013.

claim: Aven-deficient MOLT4 cells had reduced MLL1 and MLL4 protein levels.
source: Both MLL1 and MLL4 protein levels were reduced in Aven-deficient MOLT4 and CCRF-CEM cells (Figure 6A,B), whereas the levels of corresponding mRNAs remained unchanged (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Aven-deficient CCRF-CEM cells had reduced MLL1 and MLL4 protein levels.
